author: bryclevgp
title: Hold a priority's results back until it has a good read
body:
A priority's results page and its agent would talk about themes, splits and "most said" after a handful of replies. That reads as a finding when it is a few people who chose to answer, and an official can act on it. Bryan's rule: until a priority has a good read, show who answered and how far there is to go, and hold the read back.

For now a good read is the priority's pooled answers (the results page's "who answered" count across texts, calls and doors) reaching `answersNeeded` for the district's census population, the same figure Serve onboarding tells officials about. Census closeness will join it later with weighting, so the decision lives in one function in gp-api (`priorityReadStatus`, returning `{ answers, needed, good }`) and every surface reads its result: a light `GET /v1/priorities/:id/read-status`, `readStatus` on the results response, the priority flow's `<priority>` block and the Chief of Staff's `<priorities>`. The population comes from the single-row census lookup the district stats already run, not the voter scan, and is memoized per district because the page and every turn ask for it.

Everything is behind `serve-citizen-panels`:

- On a phone the priority gets a short bar instead of the scrolling header: back, the title on one line, and a list button for "Where this stands". Under it one row: how many more answers a good read needs, with a bar and Get answers, or "You have a good read" and See what we heard. The row text and bar open the results page. This uses as little height as it can so the conversation keeps the screen.
- On desktop the same line, bar and button sit at the top of the rail, with a quiet "What we heard" link, then "Where this stands". Nothing goes above the chat.
- Get answers sends the agent one hidden turn (a new contracts marker, like the report back and sent-from-a-card turns) asking it to propose more answers for the check that is out. The agent offers a card; nothing sends from the button. The results page's Get answers links back to the priority and triggers the same turn once.
- The results page stays reachable. Before a good read it shows who answered by channel and the answers still needed, and holds the themes, map and census comparison behind one line.
- The priority agent and the Chief of Staff share no results before a good read. They nudge toward more answers, and a direct "what have people said" gets an honest sentence or two and "too early to act on". Reporting back to the people a text asked is left as is: it tells those people what they said, not what the district thinks. The prompt change is its own block (`buildGoodReadBlock`), apart from the sampling and proposal sizing being changed elsewhere.

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes what officials and LLM agents can see and say about early priority feedback, plus new API and chat behavior behind a feature flag; incorrect read thresholds could mis-gate UI and agent guidance.
> 
> **Overview**
> Introduces a **good read** gate for priority constituent feedback: pooled answers across channels must reach district-sized `answersNeeded` before themes and district-level reads are treated as actionable. gp-api centralizes that in `priorityReadStatus`, exposes `GET /v1/priorities/:id/read-status` and embeds `readStatus` on priority results (district census population via memoized lookup, 96 fallback when unknown).
> 
> Behind **`serve-citizen-panels`**, the priority workspace shows progress (bar, **Get answers**) on mobile and in the desktop rail; **Get answers** sends a hidden `[Get answers]` chat turn so the agent proposes more outreach without auto-sending. The **What we heard** results page keeps themes, map, and census comparison hidden until `good` is true. **Priority flow** and **Chief of Staff** prompts get matching **BEFORE A GOOD READ** rules (no themes/splits/quotes; honest short answer if asked directly; Get answers → outreach card).

+// The one place a "good read" is decided. Census closeness joins `good` here

+  answers: number
+  population: number | null

+    needed,
+    good: input.answers >= needed,
+  }
